cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: kurtosis of the ten-value sample 3,4,5,2,3,4,5,6,4,7
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as -0.1518. Independently derived from the documented excess-kurtosis formula n(n+1)/((n-1)(n-2)(n-3)) * SUM(((x-mean)/s)^4) - 3(n-1)^2/((n-2)(n-3)) with n = 10, mean 4.3, s = 1.4181 -> -0.15179964

cases.description: A heavy single outlier raises kurtosis above zero
cases.expected_note: Derived from the documented formula: mean 2.6, s = 3.5777; standardized deviations are four copies of -0.44721 and one of 1.78885; sum of 4th powers = 10.4; n(n+1)/((n-1)(n-2)(n-3)) = 30/24 = 1.25; 1.25*10.4 = 13; minus 3(n-1)^2/((n-2)(n-3)) = 48/6 = 8; 13-8 = 5

cases.description: The (n-3) factor is undefined below four data points
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #DIV/0! if there are fewer than four data points, because (n-3) is zero

cases.description: Identical values give a zero sample standard deviation
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #DIV/0! if the sample standard deviation of the data is zero
